requirements.note: Inset-grouped list, newest first, with a Pinned section on top. Each row shows title, short date (time for today, weekday for this week) and a one-line preview. Long titles wrap to two lines.
Filters title and body as you type and keeps the Pinned/Notes sections. But the bottom search field stays behind the keyboard, so you cannot see what you are typing or reach the clear button.
Title field and body view, no Save button. The edit saved, the date became today, and the note moved to the top of its section; it survived relaunch.
The compose button opens a blank note with the title focused. Backing out of an empty note leaves the count at 90; a note with text is kept (91).
Swipe left gives Delete; long press gives a context menu with Pin/Unpin and Delete. Both worked and persisted. There is no leading swipe for pin, and a full swipe does not delete.
'90 Notes' subtitle under the large title; it updates on create and delete.
Edits, new notes, deletes and unpins all survived relaunch.

bugs: While searching, the bottom search field does not rise above the keyboard; it stays hidden behind it, so the query and clear button cannot be seen while typing.
Dragging right across a row opens the note, as if the swipe were a tap.
In the editor, tapping into the body scrolls the content so the title slides under the floating back/pin buttons.
tells: No leading swipe action for pin, and a full left swipe only reveals Delete instead of deleting.
The Delete swipe button is narrow (63 pt) compared with the system one.
The editor title is a single-line text field that truncates long titles ('Meeting notes with the de…') instead of wrapping as Notes does.
At the largest text size the editor body breaks 'recommendatio / ns' in the middle of a word, with no hyphen.
The bottom-toolbar search field and the '90 Notes' subtitle stay small at the largest text size.
There is no Done button to dismiss the keyboard while editing.
The '90 Notes' subtitle under the large title is tiny (about 11 pt) and crowded against the title.
A.scroll: Smooth through 90 rows on slow drags and flings, with no blank or popping rows; the large title collapses inline properly, and the scroll position is kept after returning from a note.

requirements.note: Native-looking inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, newest first. Each row shows title, short date (time for today, weekday for this week) and a one-line preview; long titles truncate.
Search field under the large title moves into the nav bar while active and filters title and body live. The toolbar count changes to '18 Found'.

Edits save without a button, the date becomes today, the note moves to the top, and it persisted. But the editor layout is broken: the date label fills most of the screen and pushes the title and body to the bottom. In dark mode they were entirely off-screen until scrolled.

Compose button in the bottom toolbar; title focused, and Return moves to the body. An empty note is discarded (stayed 90); a note with text is kept (91). The new-note title also starts low, and the body sits under the keyboard.
System swipe actions: trailing Delete, and a leading swipe that toggles pin (a full swipe unpinned a note). A long-press menu also has Unpin Note and Delete. Both persisted.
'91 Notes' in the bottom toolbar, as in Apple Notes; it becomes 'N Found' while searching.
Edits, new notes and pin changes survived relaunch.

bugs: In the note editor, the date label takes up hundreds of points, so a short note's title and body sit at the bottom of the screen or below it. Opening a note shows a mostly blank page and you must scroll to reach the text; on a new note the body field is under the keyboard. It only lays out correctly when the text is long enough to fill the screen (e.g. at the largest text size).
Tapping the body area of a just-opened note, where the body is clipped at the bottom edge, did not focus it.
tells: The editor's huge empty space with the date floating mid-screen looks nothing like a system notes editor.
The toolbar count text stays small at the largest text size (minor, and it matches the system).
B.scroll: Smooth and native: slow drags, flings and fling-back to the top are clean, with no blank rows, the large title collapses with the search field, and the scroll position is kept after returning from a note.

why: B's list, search and swipe actions are more native than A's, but its note editor, the core screen of a notes app, is badly laid out: every short note opens to a blank page with the text pushed to the bottom or off-screen. A has its own clear flaws (the search field hidden under the keyboard, no leading swipe, a mid-word break at large text), but editing notes in A works and looks right, so it is narrowly the one I'd rather use.
